Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa (Salesforce PWA Kit v3 on @salesforce/retail-react-app v10, TypeScript-only inside overrides/).

I am estimating FED (front-end) effort for a story: "Checkout – Reduce Login Friction via Email & OTP" — shopper enters email, receives a 6-digit one-time passcode by email, enters it into 6 digit boxes with a 5:00 countdown + RESEND link + "USE A DIFFERENT EMAIL" link, in a login DRAWER (not a modal/page).

Investigate very thoroughly and report EVIDENCE with absolute file paths + line numbers. Answer these specific questions:

1. **Base SFCC passwordless support**: Read in full:
   - node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/passwordless-login/index.jsx
   - node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/auth-utils.js
   - node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/login/index.jsx
   - node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/login/passwordless-landing.jsx (and .test.js)
   - node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/email-confirmation/index.jsx
   - node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.js
   - node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout/partials/login-state.jsx and contact-info.jsx
   - node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout-one-click/** (this looks like an SFCC OOTB low-friction checkout — is it passwordless/OTP based? Summarise what it gives.)

   KEY QUESTION: Is the OOTB SLAS passwordless flow a **magic link** (emailed clickable URL → callback/landing page) or a **6-digit code the user types in**? Quote the exact code/constants that prove it. Look for `callback_uri`, `mode`, `PASSWORDLESS`, `pwdless`, `usid`, `authorizePasswordless`, `getPasswordLessAccessToken`, `loginRegisteredUserB2C`, `token` exchange. Check what SLAS `mode` values the SDK supports — grep node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic and node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react for `passwordless`, `mode`, `callback_uri`, `sms`.

2. **What Zimmermann already has in overrides/**: read in full:
   - overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.tsx
   - overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmAuthDrawerContent/index.tsx (+ errorFallback.tsx)
   - overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx
   - overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts
   Tell me: does a login DRAWER already exist and work? What steps/screens does it already have (email entry? password? register?)? Does it already do passwordless? What atoms does it reuse (ZimmTextInput, ZimmButton, ZimmDrawer)?

3. **Reusable atoms/molecules that a 6-digit OTP input could reuse**: list what exists under overrides/app/components/ui-kits/ (atoms, molecules, organisms) — give me the full directory listing of component folder names. Specifically: is there any PIN/code/segmented input, any countdown/timer component, any resend-link pattern? Does Chakra UI's version in this repo ship `PinInput`/`HStack` (check node_modules/@chakra-ui/react version and whether PinInput is exported)?

4. **Does overrides/ have a checkout login step override at all?** List every file under overrides/app/pages/checkout/ and say what is overridden vs still base. Is `login-state.jsx`/`contact-info.jsx` overridden?

5. Grep the whole repo (excluding node_modules) for: `passwordless`, `PinInput`, `otp`, `OTP`, `resend`, `countdown`, `SLAS`. Report real hits with paths.

Be precise and factual. Do not speculate. If something does not exist, say so explicitly.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

    28	import {useCurrentCustomer} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-customer'
    29	import {useOtpInputs} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-otp-inputs'

    31	import {getConfig} from '@salesforce/pwa-kit-runtime/utils/ssr-config'
    32	
    33	const OtpAuth = ({
    34	    isOpen,
    35	    onClose,
    36	    form,
    37	    handleSendEmailOtp,
    38	    handleOtpVerification,
    39	    onCheckoutAsGuest,
    40	    isGuestRegistration = false,
    41	    hideCheckoutAsGuestButton = false,
    42	    resendCooldownDuration = 30
    43	}) => {
    44	    const {tokenLength} = getConfig().app.login
    45	    const parsedLength = Number(tokenLength)
    46	    const isValidOtpLength = parsedLength === 6 || parsedLength === 8
    47	    const OTP_LENGTH = isValidOtpLength ? parsedLength : 8
    48	
    49	    if (!isValidOtpLength) {
    50	        console.warn(
    51	            `Invalid OTP token length: ${tokenLength}. Expected 6 or 8. Defaulting to ${OTP_LENGTH}.`
    52	        )
    53	    }
    54	
    55	    const [isVerifying, setIsVerifying] = useState(false)
    56	    const [error, setError] = useState('')
    57	    const [resendTimer, setResendTimer] = useCountdown(0)
    58	
    59	    // Privacy-aware user identification hooks
    60	    const {getUsidWhenReady} = useUsid()
    61	    const {isRegistered} = useCustomerType()
    62	    const {data: customer} = useCurrentCustomer()
    63	    const {effectiveDnt} = useDNT()
    64	
    65	    // Einstein tracking
    66	    const {sendViewPage} = useEinstein()
    67	
    68	    // Get privacy-compliant user identifier
    69	    const getUserIdentifier = async () => {
    70	        // Respect Do Not Track
    71	        if (effectiveDnt) {
    72	            return '__DNT__'
    73	        }
    74	        // Use customer ID for registered users
    75	        if (isRegistered && customer?.customerId) {
    76	            return customer.customerId
    77	        }
    78	        // Use USID for guest users
    79	        const usid = await getUsidWhenReady()
    80	        return usid
    81	    }
    82	
    83	    const track = async (path, payload = {}) => {
    84	        const userId = await getUserIdentifier()
    85	        sendViewPage(path, {
    86	            userId,
    87	            userType: isRegistered ? 'registered' : 'guest',
    88	            dntCompliant: effectiveDnt,
    89	            ...payload
    90	        })
    91	    }
    92	
    93	    const otpInputs = useOtpInputs(OTP_LENGTH, (code) => {
    94	        if (code.length === OTP_LENGTH) {
    95	            handleVerify(code)
    96	        }
    97	    })

    99	    useEffect(() => {
   100	        if (isOpen) {
   101	            otpInputs.clear()
   102	            setError('')
   103	            form.setValue('otp', '')
   104	            // Start resend cooldown when modal opens
   105	            setResendTimer(resendCooldownDuration)
   106	
   107	            // Track OTP modal view activity
   108	            track('/otp-authentication', {
   109	                activity: 'otp_modal_viewed',
   110	                context: 'authentication'
   111	            })
   112	
   113	            setTimeout(() => otpInputs.inputRefs.current[0]?.focus(), 100)
   114	        }
   115	    }, [isOpen, resendCooldownDuration])
   116	
   117	    const handleVerify = async (code = otpInputs.values.join('')) => {
   118	        if (isVerifying || code.length !== OTP_LENGTH) return
   119	
   120	        setIsVerifying(true)
   121	        setError('')
   122	
   123	        // Track OTP verification attempt
   124	        track('/otp-verification', {
   125	            activity: 'otp_verification_attempted',
   126	            context: 'authentication',
   127	            otpLength: code.length
   128	        })

   130	        try {

   134	                otpInputs.clear()

   137	                track('/otp-verification-failed', {
   138	                    activity: 'otp_verification_failed',
   139	                    context: 'authentication',
   140	                    error: result.error
   141	                })
   142	            }
   143	        } finally {

   147	                activity: 'otp_verification_successful',
   148	                context: 'authentication'
   149	            })
   150	        }
   151	    }
   152	
   153	    const handleResend = async () => {
   154	        // No action while verifying or during cooldown; button stays visible/enabled
   155	        if (isVerifying || resendTimer > 0) return
   156	
   157	        setResendTimer(resendCooldownDuration)

   161	                context: 'authentication',
   162	                resendAttempt: true
   163	            })

   168	                activity: 'otp_resend_failed',
   169	                context: 'authentication',
   170	                error: error.message
   171	            })

   173	        }
   174	    }
   175	
   176	    const handleCheckoutAsGuest = async () => {
   177	        if (isVerifying) return

   180	        await track('/checkout-as-guest', {
   181	            activity: 'checkout_as_guest_selected',
   182	            context: 'otp_authentication',
   183	            userChoice: 'guest_checkout'
   184	        })

   186	        if (onCheckoutAsGuest) {

   188	        }
   189	        onClose()
   190	    }
   191	
   192	    const handleInputChange = (index, value) => {
   193	        const code = otpInputs.setValue(index, value)
   194	        setError('') // Clear error on user input
   195	        if (typeof code === 'string') {
   196	            form.setValue('otp', code)

   202	
   203	    return (
   204	        <Modal isOpen={isOpen} onClose={onClose} isCentered size="lg" closeOnOverlayClick={false}>
   205	            <ModalOverlay />
   206	            <ModalContent>
   207	                <ModalHeader>

   209	                        <FormattedMessage
   210	                            defaultMessage="Create an account"
   211	                            id="otp.title.create_account"
   212	                        />
   213	                    ) : (
   214	                        <FormattedMessage
   215	                            defaultMessage="Confirm it's you"
   216	                            id="otp.title.confirm_its_you"
   217	                        />
   218	                    )}
   219	                </ModalHeader>
   220	                <ModalCloseButton disabled={isVerifying} />
   221	                <ModalBody pb={6}>
   222	                    <Stack spacing={12} paddingLeft={4} paddingRight={4} alignItems="center">
   223	                        <Text fontSize="md" maxWidth={80} textAlign="center">
   224	                            {isGuestRegistration ? (
   225	                                <FormattedMessage
   226	                                    defaultMessage="We sent a one-time password (OTP) to your email. To create your account and proceed to checkout, enter the {otpLength}-digit code below."
   227	                                    id="otp.message.enter_code_for_account_guest"
   228	                                    values={{otpLength: OTP_LENGTH}}

   235	                            )}
   236	                        </Text>
   237	
   238	                        <Stack spacing={6} width="100%" alignItems="center">
   239	                            {/* OTP Input */}
   240	                            <SimpleGrid columns={OTP_LENGTH} spacing={3}>

   242	                                    <Input
   243	                                        key={index}
   244	                                        ref={(el) => (otpInputs.inputRefs.current[index] = el)}

   249	                                        type="text"

   252	                                        textAlign="center"
   253	                                        fontSize="lg"
   254	                                        fontWeight="bold"
   255	                                        size="lg"
   256	                                        width={12}
   257	                                        height={14}
   258	                                        borderRadius="md"
   259	                                        borderColor={error ? 'red.500' : 'gray.300'}
   260	                                        borderWidth={2}
   261	                                        disabled={isVerifying}
   262	                                        _focus={{
   263	                                            borderColor: error ? 'red.500' : 'blue.500',

   266	                                                : '0 0 0 1px var(--chakra-colors-blue-500)'
   267	                                        }}
   268	                                        _hover={{
   269	                                            borderColor: error ? 'red.500' : 'gray.400'
   270	                                        }}
   271	                                    />
   272	                                ))}
   273	                            </SimpleGrid>
   274	
   275	                            {/* Loading spinner during verification */}
   276	                            {isVerifying && (

   279	                                    color="blue.500"

   289	                                    {error}

   291	                            )}
   292	
   293	                            {/* Countdown message */}
   294	                            {resendTimer > 0 && (
   295	                                <Text fontSize="sm" color="gray.600" textAlign="center">
   296	                                    <FormattedMessage
   297	                                        defaultMessage="You can request a new code in {timer} {timer, plural, one {second} other {seconds}}."
   298	                                        id="otp.message.resend_cooldown"
   299	                                        values={{timer: resendTimer}}
   300	                                    />
   301	                                </Text>
   302	                            )}
   303

   305	                            <HStack spacing={4} width="100%" justifyContent="center">

content.text: ## Headline **Almost everything this story needs already exists and already works in this repo.** A Zimmermann-branded login **drawer** with email entry + "Send code" is live (wishlist auth gate), and it already drives the full SLAS passwordless **typed-OTP** round-trip. The real FED delta is: (a) move the OTP step **out of SFCC's modal and into the drawer**, (b) build a Zimmermann 6-box OTP input + 5:00 countdown + RESEND + "USE A DIFFERENT EMAIL", (c) **wire it into checkout, which is 100% un-overridden today**. --- ## 1. Base SFCC passwordless support ### THE KEY ANSWER: it is **both** — `mode` decides, and this repo is already set to the typed-code path `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react@5.2.0` — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/auth/index.d.ts:47-59` ```ts type AuthorizePasswordlessParams = { callbackURI?: string; userid: string; mode?: 'email' | 'callback'; locale?: string; register_customer?: boolean | string; // SLAS registers the customer as part of the flow ... }; type GetPasswordLessAccessTokenParams = { // line 61 pwdlessLoginToken: string; register_customer?: boolean | string; }; ``` The SDK union is **exactly two values: `'email' | 'callback'`**. There is **no `'sms'` mode in the TypeScript surface** — `sms` appears only in SLAS API prose in `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts:1427, 1442, 1478, 1504, 1518` ("Required when the mode is `email` or `sms`"). Do not plan for SMS. Wire shapes, `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.cjs.d.ts`: - `authorizePasswordlessCustomerBodyType` (~line 564): `user_id`, `mode`, `locale`, `usid`, `channel_id`, `callback_uri?` (line 570), `register_customer` fields - `getPasswordLessAccessTokenBodyType` (~line 644): `grant_type`, `hint`, **`pwdless_login_token`** (line 648), `client_id?`, `code_verifier?`, `login_id?` - Line 1445 proves `callback_uri` is **only** for magic-link mode: *"The callback URI. **Required when the mode is `callback`**… must be a `POST` endpoint because the token will be included in the body."* - Line 1997: *"`pwdless_login_token` — Passwordless login token that was created from the user ID."* - Line 1519: `grant_type` = `passwordless_login_pkce`; scope `sfcc.pwdless_login` **So:** | mode | What SLAS does | Base UI | |---|---|---| | `'email'` | Emails a **TOTP code the shopper types in** | `components/otp-auth` (digit boxes) | | `'callback'` | POSTs the token to your `callback_uri` → magic link / landing page | `components/email-confirmation` ("Resend **Link**") + `landingPath` route | **This repo is already on `mode: 'email'`** — `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/config/default.js:91`, with `callbackURI` **commented out** at lines 94-95. Passwordless is `enabled: true` in every named tier (`config/dev.js:11-14`, and identically in `sit.js`, `uat.js`, `staging.js`, `production.js`, `test.js` — all at lines 9-19). ### The single most important file you didn't ask about: `components/otp-auth` `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa/node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/otp-auth/index.jsx` — 374 lines. This is a **complete, working, typed-6-digit OTP UI**: - Line 44-53: `OTP_LENGTH` from `getConfig().app.login.tokenLength`; **accepts only 6 or 8**, defaults 8, `console.warn` otherwise - Line 240-273: `` of individual `` — **this is the 6-box segmented input, hand-rolled, not Chakra PinInput** - Line 93-97 + 117-151: auto-submit as soon as the last digit lands - Line 57 + 294-302: countdown text, `resendCooldownDuration` prop — **default 30 seconds, not 5:00** - Line 153-174 + 338-351: `handleResend` + "Resend Code" **button** (not a link), no-op while `resendTimer > 0` - Line 306-336: optional "Checkout as a Guest" / "Cancel" button (`hideCheckoutAsGuestButton`) - Line 204: wrapped in a Chakra **``** — hard-coded, not swappable Supporting hooks (both tiny, both reusable as-is): - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-otp-inputs.js` — 59 lines: digits-only guard, auto-advance, backspace-to-previous, full paste handling - `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-countdown.js` — 20 lines: `[count, setCount]`, `setTimeout` 1s decrement ### The other base files you listed - **`components/passwordless-login/index.jsx`** (105 lines) — email-only fields + "Continue" + a "Password" toggle to `StandardLogin` + social. **No OTP, no countdown, no resend.** Nothing here for this story. - **`components/email-confirmation/index.jsx`** (93 lines) — this is the **magic-link** screen: line 60 `"We just sent a login link to {email}"`, line 78 `"Resend Link"`. **Wrong mode for this story; do not reuse.** - **`pages/login/passwordless-landing.jsx` — DOES NOT EXIST.** Only `passwordless-landing.test.js` exists (8381 bytes), and it imports `Login from '.'` (line 14) — the "landing page" is just `pages/login/index.jsx` mounted at `landingPath`. Confirmed in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/routes.jsx:147-152`. - **`pages/login/index.jsx`** (233 lines) — `handlePasswordlessLogin` at 110-123 sends `{userid, mode, locale, callbackURI?}` then `setIsOtpAuthOpen(true)`; `handleOtpVerification` at 125-134 calls `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync({pwdlessLoginToken})`. Lines 159-170 read `?token=` from the query string — **that branch is the `callback`/magic-link path and is dead code here** since `landingPath` is only routed when configured and `mode` is `'email'`. - **`hooks/use-auth-modal.js`** (415 lines) — Chakra `Modal` with 4 views (`login`/`register`/`password`/`email`), and `` rendered as a **sibling** at lines 372-379. Line 163-167: closes the AuthModal, waits 150ms, then opens the OTP modal. - **`pages/checkout/partials/login-state.jsx`** (116 lines) — a "**Secure Link**" outline button (line 46-49) alongside "Password" and social. - **`pages/checkout/partials/contact-info.jsx`** (333 lines) — **this is the gap.** Line 89-104: on passwordless click it fires `authorizePasswordlessLogin`, then `setAuthModalView(EMAIL_VIEW)` + `authModal.onOpen()` → which renders `PasswordlessEmailConfirmation`, i.e. **the "Check Your Email / Resend Link" magic-link screen**. Base checkout **never renders `OtpAuth`**. Its copy is wrong for `mode: 'email'` out of the box. ### `checkout-one-click/**` — what it actually is **Not** a passwordless/OTP product. It is an express **saved-shipping/saved-payment** checkout for returning shoppers (33 files under `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/checkout-one-click/`). Base `routes.jsx:82-88` swaps it in for `/checkout` when `oneClickCheckout.enabled` — **which is `false` in `config/default.js:172`**, so it is inert in this repo. **But it is the best OOTB reference implementation of exactly this story**, because `pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-contact-info.jsx` is the only base checkout file that wires OTP properly: - line 41 imports `OtpAuth`; line 699-705 renders it with `handleSendEmailOtp` / `handleOtpVerification` / **`onCheckoutAsGuest`** - line 221 `handleSendEmailOtp(email, isResend)`; line 245-247 `authorizePasswordlessLogin.mutateAsync({..., mode: passwordlessConfig?.mode})` - line 260-268 handles "guest not found" → registration branch (`isGuestRegistration`) - line 303-307 `handleOtpVerification` → `loginPasswordless.mutateAsync({pwdlessLoginToken: otpCode})` - line 105-108 single-flight guard `otpSendPromiseRef` + `lastEmailSentRef` to stop duplicate sends Note `one-click-login-state.jsx` (37 lines) dropped the passwordless button entirely — social only.
